parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian бу́да (búda), from Old Polish buda, from Middle High German buode.

parole.significato: to hold back, to restrain, to contain, to check, to subdue, to repress, to temper, to withhold
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian гамовати (hamovati) (since the early XVI), from Old Polish hamować, from Middle High German hamen, from Old High German *hamōn. Compare modern German hemmen, from Proto-West Germanic *hammjan, whence also English hem.

Inherited from Middle Ukrainian гетьманъ m (hetʹman), гетманъ m (hetman), from Old Polish hethman m, probably from Middle High German houbetman, heuptman (“commander”), from houbet, heupt (“head”), related to Latin caput (“head”), + Middle High German man (“man”). Compare Modern Polish hetman m and
Inherited from Old Ruthenian зекгаръ (zegar), дзикгаръ (dzigar), from Old Polish zegar, zygar, from Middle High German seigære. Compare Polish zegar.

Inherited from Middle Ukrainian кушнѣръ (kušnir), from earlier кушнеръ (kušner), from Old Polish kusznierz, from Middle High German kürsenære, from Old High German kursināri, from Old High German kursina, from Proto-Slavic *kъrzьno, whence Ukrainian ко́рзно (kórzno).

parole.significato: to torture, to torment, to rack, to excruciate (inflict severe physical pain or mental suffering on)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian мордова́ти (mordováti, “to torture, to torment”), from Old Polish mordować (“to murder”), from Middle High German morden, mörden, mürden (“to murder”), from Old High German morden, murden (“to murder”), from Proto-West Germanic *murþijan (“to murder”), from Proto-Germani

Inherited from Old Ruthenian му́сити (músiti), from Old Polish musić, from Middle High German müeȥen, from Old High German muoȥan, from Proto-West Germanic *mōtan, from Proto-Germanic *mōtaną (whence German müssen and English must). Compare loans from the same source Belarusian му́сіць (músicʹ), Cze

parole.significato: to hit (to manage to touch (a target) in the right place)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian тра́пити (trápiti), from Old Polish trapić, trafić, from Middle High German treffan, from Old High German treffan, from Proto-West Germanic *drepan, from Proto-Germanic *drepaną, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰreb-, *dʰrebʰ- (“to grind; crush; kill”), whence also Ukrainian
Inherited from Old Ruthenian цыбу́лѧ, цибу́лѧ (cybúlja, cibúlja), from Old Polish cybula, from Middle High German zibolle, zebülle, zwibole, from Late Latin cepulla, from Latin cepa.
From Middle Ukrainian кгвалтъ (gvalt), гвалтъ (hvalt), ґвалтъ (gvalt), through Old Polish gwałt (Polish gwałt), from Middle High German gewalt (“strength, power”).
